## Fixed

- `structured` reads a ruled table whose rules are drawn many to a path.
  Acrobat's export of a spreadsheet draws a whole row of column rules, or a
  run of row rules, as one path of thin rectangles; the toolkit took each path
  by its bounds, one box over all of them, so no grid was found and the table
  was read from text alignment. A use matrix with rotated district headers and
  mostly blank cells (St. Johns County FL, Land Development Code Article II,
  Table 2.03.01) came out as unordered runs of `A`/`S` with the blank cells
  dropped, so no value could be tied to its district. Each closed, axis-aligned
  rectangle of such a path is now read on its own: a thin one is a rule, an
  outlined one frames a cell. What the path fills is still read by its extent,
  as before, so a column of panels drawn as one path stays one panel.

  The table now reads with one column per district and every blank cell kept.
  A page of it joins the text bench (`stjohns-ldc2-p39-use-table`, 253 cells);
  the bench is 1459 of 1459 checks, against 0 of the new page's 253 for 0.19.3.
  Over 129 local documents (12,989 pages), `structured` markdown changes on 53
  pages of 10 documents: the dimensional and noise tables of the Village of
  Beach Park's zoning code read as tables with their headers (they were runs
  of bold text), a Miami 21 frontage description reads whole, and a diagram
  of two crossing road lines on one page now reads as a two-cell grid. The
  text ledgers, scorecard and dossier annotations are unchanged.
